clue.text: Cook holding plate in acknowledgment

the L-plate shown by a British learner driver

explanation.surface: A chef raises a plate in thanks, like a toast to the diners.
explanation.walkthrough: SAUTE holds L to give SALUTE. An L-plate is the red-on-white L sign a British learner driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: A salute is a gesture of greeting or recognition, such as a raised hand to an officer.

clue.text: Time out before rounds

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sports timekeeper calling a break before play resumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time out' reads as one phrase, but 'Time' is the first meaning and 'out before rounds' describes boxing helpers who step out of the ring as the bell goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Seconds measure duration in clocks, and in boxing the seconds are corner assistants who climb out between bouts.

clue.text: After 22, 29 15 his

setter's reading: in Jaques's Seven Ages speech the third age follows the schoolboy, and the proverb says all the world loves one

explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the cross-references: after the SCHOOLBOY comes the third age, and 'All the world's his' nods to the saying that all the world loves a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It, Jaques lists infant, schoolboy, then the sighing romantic who writes ballads to his mistress's eyebrow.

clue.text: Zaire tram refurbished in poetic form

indicators.note: something refurbished is taken apart and put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old African streetcar is being done up, and the result is described as poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Terza rima is the interlocking three-line rhyme scheme Dante used in the Divine Comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Terza rima is a verse pattern of tercets rhyming aba bcb cdc, so it is a named poetic structure.

clue.text: Nothing but diamonds after 13

explanation.surface: A card player declaring a hand of only diamonds, following on from another bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is SOLDIER; in Jaques's Seven Ages speech the soldier is followed by the justice, the fat magistrate full of wise saws.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth of Shakespeare's seven ages, coming straight after the soldier, is the well-fed magistrate or judge.

clue.text: Recently obtained present at the fair?

parts.note: just means fair, as in a just ruling
the present moment is now

explanation.surface: Someone has just picked up a gift at a funfair stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift and 'fair' a funfair; read as the present time and as equitable, they give the two words, with fair coming first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something happened a moment ago, only a short while back, is a plain synonym phrase for recently.

clue.text: Cuttlefish's relation in water

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first piece goes within the second

explanation.surface: A cuttlefish has a cousin living somewhere in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' wants to be a family member; here it is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter. 'Cuttlefish's' is read as 'cuttlefish is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the zoological genus name of the common cuttlefish, and also the brown ink it squirts.

clue.text: Cuttlefish well, perhaps: elk or hind poorly

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vet's report: the cuttlefish is well, but the deer are ailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like healthy, but it is an inkwell; a cuttlefish carries its own ink sac, so it is an example of the answer, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkwell is a pot for ink, and a cuttlefish with its ink sac is a living one, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Message the Queen carried to the Duke

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher
a newspaper that carried a story ran it

explanation.surface: A royal messenger takes a note from the Queen to a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the standard abbreviation for the Queen, from Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand was originally a message or mission entrusted to someone, an older sense still found in 'a fool's errand'.

clue.text: Port or cocktail causes semi-comatose state

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Too much fortified wine or mixed drinks leaves a drinker half unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor is sluggish inactivity or stupor, a sleepy state close to unconsciousness.

clue.text: Number 0 in hell, deep and hollow

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: something placed in a place is put inside it, so the figure goes within the next piece

the zero digit read as the letter O

explanation.surface: A grim description of an empty, bottomless pit in hell.
explanation.walkthrough: C begins the answer; O goes inside AVERNUS. Avernus is a classical name for the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavernous describes something like a cave: vast, deep and empty inside, as in a cavernous hall.

clue.text: Game on the hearth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a card game played for stakes
second meaning: the iron rod kept by the fireplace for stirring coals

explanation.surface: A family playing a board game in front of the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a gambling card game and the metal fire tool that lies beside the grate.

clue.text: Opera is a standard article

explanation.walkthrough: Norma is Bellini's opera about a Druid priestess.

clue.text: Acknowledgment between god and fool after 4

explanation.walkthrough: 4 is JUSTICE; in the Seven Ages speech the justice gives way to 'the lean and slipper'd pantaloon', the foolish old man of comedy.

clue.text: After 2, I come in to join with iron

indicators.note: to come in is to enter, so the single letter enters the other word

parts.note: metal is joined using a soldering iron
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone joining a metalwork job after a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is LOVER; Jaques's fourth age is the soldier, full of strange oaths. 'Iron' looks like the metal but is the hot tool used to join wires.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Seven Ages speech the sighing romantic is followed by the bearded fighting man seeking reputation at the cannon's mouth.

clue.text: Midday meal starts inside in the UCL mess

parts.note: the opening letter of meal
taken as written; UCL is University College London

explanation.walkthrough: 'Midday meal' looks like the definition, but the meal's first letter is needed in the fodder, leaving just 'Midday'. UCL is University College London.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunchtime is the hour around noon when people stop to eat, so it means the middle of the day.

clue.text: See 29

the el is the American elevated railway

explanation.surface: A new train line needs someone to set the standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New railway' suggests a model railway, but the two words are clued separately; the el is the American name for an elevated city railway such as Chicago's.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person whose behaviour others copy, so the phrase means an example or exemplar.

clue.text: Part I doing time in the cooler

parts.note: taken as written
a fan cools the air

explanation.surface: Chapter one of a prisoner's memoir about serving a sentence in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing time in the cooler' is prison slang, but the cooler is a fan. The first of Jaques's seven ages is the baby 'mewling and puking in the nurse's arms'.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening stage of life in Shakespeare's speech is the newborn baby, so it is the first part of the sequence.

clue.text: Explorer turns up with gas for pipe

clue.text: Northern light with round number in capital

a round shape like the letter O

explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern light' suggests the aurora borealis, but it is the star in the northern sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the Pole Star, sits almost directly above the North Pole and has long guided navigators.

clue.text: Film about shy characters taking medicine

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Physic is an old word for medicine, still heard in 'physic garden'.
explanation.definitionFit: Physic is an archaic term for medicinal drugs or the art of healing, as in a dose of physic.

clue.text: Warm air sent to the French is a fraud

parts.note: a south wind, which brings warm air
le is French for the

explanation.walkthrough: S is the abbreviation for south; a south wind brings warm air in the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: See 29
After 17, he's inspired by holy Bosco

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Beginning to be occupying 21?

clue.text: Ruler not of uniform habit?

clue.text: Jack's a disappointment

clue.text: Another name for animal, I assume

explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed or false name used instead of one's real one, so it is another name.
